rules.when: Tiny, fully specified work with nothing to decide: reading back a value, a one-line edit, a status check, a quick lookup, or a few such chores dispatched at once.
rules.why: Haiku 5.5 does a chore at a small fraction of Opus's usage, which leaves more of a Pro or Max 5x window for the work that needs Opus.

rules.when: Well-specified mechanical work whose specification is already precise: a rote rename, a formatting sweep, tests against existing behaviour, documentation generated from a diff, or several such tasks dispatched at once.
rules.why: Sonnet 5.5 is fast and good value when the task leaves little to judgment, and a wide burst of workers spends less of a Pro or Max 5x window on it.

rules.when: High-leverage planning, architecture, diagnosis, strategy or approach selection, where the worker produces judgment rather than code.
rules.why: Spend more reasoning where a wrong direction costs the most; extra-high effort is left out because a Pro or Max 5x window runs out quickly at that depth.
